title: Identifiability Testing for Linear Causal Disentanglement under Soft Interventions
banked_reason: The delivered actual-row correction is mathematically sound, but the cold review rates it incremental (5.4 below the 7.4 field floor); the promised chamberwise covariance frontier remains open after the prescribed nonidentical bounded attempt failed.
gap_reasons: The delivered core honestly leaves the proposed all-graph non-QE positive-real projection compiler open and contains no square-mixing Cov_q=Hsoft theorem, so it substitutes terminal correction plus a pointwise fork witness for the promised covariance-frontier result.

The note proves a general terminal-copy/affine characterization of corrected actual-row compatibility, an arithmetic per-candidate algorithm, and a concrete refutation of the published Theorem 3.15, but these constitute a narrow correction rather than the advertised covariance information frontier.
Classify the projected feasible union of all eight two-scalar fork systems over the full true-parameter domain and prove the resulting density or separation conclusion chamber by chamber.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the corrected actual-row terminal-copy/affine membership criterion with an O(q^4) field-operation certificate, an explicit generic counterexample to the published theorem, exact finite covariance-branch reductions, and a quotient-invariant one-parameter fork separation. The prescribed fork-only resultant/subresultant CAD attempt did not produce projection polynomials, full-dimensional sign cells, or Thom certificates, so the chamberwise density-or-separation theorem, square-mixing equality, and all-graph non-QE compiler remain open.
tldr: The headline is now exact and pointwise. Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit a sound-and-complete terminal-copy linkage and batched affine-support test in \(O(q^4)\) rational-function field operations. Definition 3.14 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal remains the published baseline-path class; the four-node determinant \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\) shows that Theorem 3.15 incorrectly identifies it with actual-row compatibility. For every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), the worked \(p=2,q=4\) fork datum has a quotient-invariant pointwise covariance realization by \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) but the actual-row obstruction \(-2\) excludes that graph from the pointwise soft set. This does not prove chamberwise density or \(\mathsf{Frontier}_2\) membership. The all-branch positive-real compiler remains open.
gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether its covariance-compatible and higher-cumulant-compatible graph classes differ, but its overcomplete example proves parameter nonuniqueness rather than a graph-specific positive-real frontier. The robust class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) refines the genericity requirement chamber by chamber, is definitionally contained in \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\), and is not identified with the published covariance-compatible class. Existing positive-semidefinite compatibility, affine-birational constraint transfer, half-trek criteria, equivalence-class recovery from unpaired interventions, and treewidth-accelerated general quantifier elimination do not decide the coupled noninjective branch union with the required realization-or-separator output. In the same paper, Equation (20) correctly derives compatibility from actual intervention rows, but the proof of Theorem 3.15 reaches the baseline-path class in Definition 3.14 by a nongeneric identification of independent change and baseline variables.
fill: The paper first proves the complete eight-branch \(p=2,q=4\) classification, then a realization-or-separator compiler for bounded covariance-terminal width with explicit certificate and bit complexity, and finally poses the all-graph compiler as the sole open information-frontier question. A separate terminal-copy theorem gives the corrected actual-row compatibility test, and a four-node counterexample identifies the precise invalid specialization in Theorem 3.15.
